x: Arun Jaitley presented the first combined Budget on 1 February 2017.

s: Since which year had India a separate Railway Budget before it was merged with the Union Budget in 2017?
x: The separate Railway Budget began in 1924 and ended with its merger into the Union Budget in 2017.

s: From which year has the Union Budget been presented on 1 February?
x: The Budget date was moved to 1 February from 2017; Arun Jaitley presented the first such combined Budget on 1 February 2017.

s: Who presented the separate agriculture budget of Andhra Pradesh for 2026-27?
x: Payyavula Keshav presented the AP Budget 2026-27 on 14 February 2026, and K. Atchannaidu presented the separate agriculture budget.

s: Who presented the Interim Union Budget 2019-20, which set out a 'Vision 2030' with ten dimensions?
x: Piyush Goyal presented the Interim Budget on 1 February 2019 and laid out ten dimensions of Vision 2030.

s: The first dimension of 'Vision 2030' in the Interim Union Budget 2019-20 aimed at infrastructure for an economy of what size?
x: The first dimension was to build physical and social infrastructure for a USD 10 trillion economy and to provide ease of living.

s: On which date was the first Union Budget of independent India presented?
x: R.K. Shanmukham Chetty presented the first Union Budget of independent India on 26 November 1947.

s: Which body prepares the Annual Financial Statement (Budget) of the Union?
o: Budget Division, Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance
Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance
x: The Budget Division of the Department of Economic Affairs in the Ministry of Finance prepares the Annual Financial Statement (Article 112).

s: Under which Article is the Public Account of India constituted?
x: The Public Account is under Article 266(2); the Consolidated Fund is under 266(1) and the Contingency Fund under 267(1).

s: On whose authority can money be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India?
o: an appropriation law passed by Parliament
x: The President cannot withdraw money alone; Article 114 requires a law of Parliament (the Appropriation Act).

s: To which fund are savings bank deposits held by the Government in trust credited?
x: Savings bank deposits are held in trust in the Public Account; treasury bills, market loans and foreign loans go to the CFI.

s: Which of the following forms part of the Consolidated Fund of India?
o: Treasury Bills raised by the Union Government
x: The CFI comprises Union revenues, loans raised (including Treasury Bills) and loan repayments; provident funds, small savings and remittances go to the Public Account.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Public Account of India?
o: Provident funds held in a fiduciary capacity are credited to it.
Small savings are credited to it.
Deposits and remittances are included in it.
Every withdrawal from it requires an appropriation law.
x: Withdrawal from the Public Account does not need appropriation the way withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund does.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Contingency Fund of India?
o: It is provided for under Article 267.
It was established by the Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950.
It is held by the Finance Secretary in the Department of Expenditure.
It is at the President's disposal for unforeseen expenditure pending Parliament's approval.
x: The Fund is held by the Finance Secretary in the Department of Economic Affairs, not the Department of Expenditure.

s: Who audits the Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund and Public Account of both the Union and the States?
x: The Comptroller and Auditor General audits all three funds of both the Union and the States.

s: What is the corpus of the Contingency Fund of India stated for the financial year 2021-22 onwards?
x: The corpus of the Contingency Fund of India was raised to ₹30,000 crore from the financial year 2021-22.

s: Under which Article is the Contingency Fund of a State provided for?
x: Article 267(2) provides for the State Contingency Fund; 267(1) is the Contingency Fund of India.

s: Which of the following is true of executive disbursements from the Public Account of India?
o: need no prior vote of Parliament
need the approval of the Rajya Sabha
need a joint sitting of Parliament
x: The government runs the Public Account as a banker for money held in trust, so payments need no prior vote of Parliament.

s: Who holds the Contingency Fund of India on behalf of the President?
o: Finance Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs
x: The Contingency Fund of India is held by the Finance Secretary, DEA, not the Department of Expenditure.

s: By whom was the Contingency Fund of India established?
x: Under Article 267(1), Parliament set up the Contingency Fund of India by the Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950.

s: Who controls the Public Account of India?
x: Payments from the Public Account (Article 266(2)) are made by the Executive without a vote of Parliament; the government acts as banker or trustee.

s: Under which Article does Parliament fix by law the salaries of the Speaker and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
x: Under Article 97 Parliament fixes the salaries of the Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman and Deputy Chairman, charged on the CFI.

s:
Consider the following statements about charged expenditure:
1. It cannot be discussed by either House of Parliament.
2. It is not submitted to the vote of Parliament.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Charged expenditure is not put to vote, but both Houses can discuss it.

s: Which of the following is votable expenditure and not charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?
o: Emoluments and office expenses of the President
Salaries and allowances of the Prime Minister and Union Ministers
x: The salaries of the Prime Minister and Union Ministers are votable; the other three are charged on the CFI.

s: On which fund are the pensions of High Court Judges charged?
x: High Court judges' pensions are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, not the State's.

s: What does the Third Schedule of the Constitution deal with?
o: Emoluments, allowances and privileges of office-holders
x: The Third Schedule contains the forms of oaths and affirmations; emoluments, allowances and privileges are in the Second Schedule.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the salaries and pensions of judges?
o: Salaries of Supreme Court Judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
Pensions of High Court Judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
Salaries of High Court Judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
Salaries of High Court Judges are paid from the State's Consolidated Fund
x: High Court judges' salaries come from the State's fund; only their pensions are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

s: How are the salaries and administrative expenses of the Election Commission met?
o: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
Paid from the Public Account of India
Met from the Contingency Fund of India
x: The Election Commission's salaries and running costs are voted, not charged.

s: In which capacity does the Vice-President of India draw his salary?
x: The Vice-President gets no salary as Vice-President and is paid only as Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

s: Which Article deals with the salaries and allowances of High Court Judges?
x: High Court judges' pay is under Article 221; Article 125 covers Supreme Court judges.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Ministers' salaries fall under Article 75(6); the President's under 59(3), Supreme Court judges' under 125 and the CAG's under 148(3).

s: Whose salary, pension and office expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?
x: The CAG's costs are charged; the Vice-President as such (paid as Rajya Sabha Chairman), Ministers and the Election Commission are not.

s: How are sums required to satisfy a judgment, decree or arbitral award met?
o: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
Paid from the Public Account of India
Met from the Contingency Fund of India
x: Sums for a judgment, decree or arbitral award are charged on the CFI under Article 112(3).

s: On which fund are the salaries and allowances of High Court Judges charged?
x: High Court judges' salaries are charged on the State's Consolidated Fund; the President's emoluments, Supreme Court judges' pay and debt charges are charged on the CFI.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about voted and charged expenditure?
o: The Election Commission's expenditure is votable
The salaries of the Prime Minister and Ministers are voted through Demands for Grants
The Vice-President receives a separate salary as Vice-President
The Vice-President is paid as Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
x: The Vice-President is paid only as Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and has no separate salary as Vice-President.

s: What is the position of charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund of India in Parliament?
o: Put to vote but not discussed
Not put to vote but can be discussed
Voted only in the Rajya Sabha
x: Charged expenditure is non-votable but can be discussed in both Houses.

s: From which fund are the emoluments of the Governor of a State paid?
x: Under Article 158(3), the Governor's emoluments are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.

s: When one person is Governor of two or more States, who decides the share of his emoluments to be paid by each State?
o: The Chief Ministers of those States jointly
x: Article 158(3A) says the emoluments are shared among the States in the proportion the President fixes by order.

s: Which Schedule of the Constitution contains the emoluments, allowances and privileges of the President, Governors, judges and the CAG?
x: The Second Schedule deals with emoluments, allowances and privileges; the Third Schedule has the forms of oaths.

s: At which stage are cut motions moved in the Lok Sabha?
o: the general discussion on the Budget
x: Cut motions are moved only in the Lok Sabha during voting on Demands for Grants; if passed, they signal loss of confidence.

s: Where does voting on Demands for Grants under Article 113 take place?
o: A joint sitting of both Houses
x: Only the Lok Sabha votes on Demands for Grants; the Rajya Sabha can only discuss the Budget.

s: Which of the following is NOT a stage of the normal budget process?
o: Scrutiny by Departmentally Related Standing Committees
x: Vote on account, vote of credit and exceptional grants are not stages of normal financial law-making.

s: What does the guillotine refer to in budget procedure?
o: Putting all remaining demands to vote without discussion on the last allotted day
x: On the last allotted day, the guillotine puts all remaining demands to vote without discussion.

s: By what amount does a Token Cut Motion seek to reduce a demand for grant?
x: A token cut reduces a demand by ₹100 to air a specific grievance. A policy cut reduces it to ₹1, and an economy cut by a specified amount.

s: Which of the following statements about Budget Cut Motions is incorrect?
o: A Policy Cut Motion seeks to reduce the demand by a specified amount.
A Token Cut Motion ventilates a specific grievance within government responsibility.
A Policy Cut Motion represents complete disapproval of the underlying policy.
An Economy Cut Motion seeks to achieve administrative economy.
x: Option A is incorrect: a policy cut reduces a demand to ₹1, showing complete disapproval of the policy. A reduction by a specified amount is an economy cut.

s: What is the parliamentary consequence of the passage of any Cut Motion in the Lok Sabha?
o: The Government is obliged to resign.
The Government is required to introduce a Confidence Motion immediately.
The matter is referred to the Committee of Privileges.
The debate is merely extended for one hour.
x: A cut motion passed in the Lok Sabha shows the government has lost financial control, which amounts to a loss of confidence, so it must resign.

s: How does a Policy Cut Motion reduce a demand for grant?
x: A policy cut reduces the demand to Re 1 to show complete disapproval of the policy behind it.

s: Which cut motion reduces a demand by a specified amount to seek economy in expenditure?
x: An economy cut reduces the demand by a specified amount; a token cut reduces it by Rs 100 to air a grievance.

s: What is it called when all remaining demands are put to vote without discussion on the last allotted day?
x: The guillotine puts all remaining demands to vote without discussion on the last day allotted.

s: To what amount does a policy cut motion reduce a demand for grant?
x: A policy cut reduces the demand to Re 1 to show disapproval of the policy; a token cut reduces it by Rs 100.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Cut motion)
A. Policy cut
B. Economy cut
C. Token cut
List-II (Reduction of the demand)
1. By Rs 100
2. To Re 1
3. By a specified amount
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: A policy cut reduces the demand to Re 1, an economy cut by a specified amount and a token cut by Rs 100.

s: Which of the following pairs of cut motions is correctly matched?
o: Policy cut – Reduction of the demand by Rs 100
Token cut – Reduction of the demand to Re 1
Economy cut – Reduction by a specified amount
Policy cut – Reduction by a specified amount
x: An economy cut reduces the demand by a specified amount; a policy cut reduces it to Re 1 and a token cut by Rs 100.

s: By how much does a token cut motion reduce a demand for grant?
x: A token cut reduces the demand by Rs 100 to air a specific grievance; a policy cut reduces it to Re 1.

s: Which provision requires an Appropriation Act for every withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of India, even for charged expenditure?
x: Article 114(3) requires an Appropriation Act for every withdrawal, so even charged expenditure, which is not voted, needs one.

s: What is the position of an amendment to the Appropriation Bill that varies the amount of expenditure charged on the CFI?
o: permitted in the Lok Sabha only
x: No amendment may vary a voted grant or charged expenditure; the Appropriation Bill also carries an automatic repeal clause.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Appropriation Bill:
1. It may authorise withdrawal of more than the amount in the Annual Financial Statement.
2. No amendment may alter the destination of a voted grant.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: No amendment may vary the amount or destination of a voted grant, and withdrawals cannot exceed the AFS amount.

s: What kind of Bill is the Appropriation Bill?
x: The Appropriation Bill is a Money Bill; the Finance Bill puts the Budget's tax proposals into effect.

s: Which of the following Bills carries an automatic repeal clause?
x: The Appropriation Bill carries an automatic repeal clause, as noted in the APPSC Group 1 Prelims 2024 question on budget enactment.

s: Which of the following amendments can be moved to the Finance Bill?
o: An amendment to increase a tax
An amendment to impose a new tax
An amendment to reduce or abolish a tax
An amendment to alter the destination of a voted grant
x: Amendments to the Finance Bill may reduce or abolish a tax but not increase it.

s: With which Article is the second batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants for 2025-26, approved by the Lok Sabha, associated?
x: Supplementary, additional or excess grants are provided for under Article 115. The second batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants for 2025-26 was approved by the Lok Sabha.

s: What is an advance grant for part of a financial year, pending passage of the Budget, called?
x: A vote on account is an advance grant for part of the year; the Appropriation Bill authorises withdrawals for voted grants and charged expenditure.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about a vote on account?
o: It is an advance for part of the year, generally about two months, until the Appropriation Act is passed.
In election years it may cover three to five months.
Since the Budget moved to 1 February (2017), it is needed in every regular Budget year.
x: Since the 1 February Budget, a vote on account is usually needed only in interim-Budget years.

s: When does an excess grant become relevant?
o: The expenditure is not part of the current service of any year
A new service is proposed in the current Budget
The sanctioned amount is insufficient before expenditure is incurred
Expenditure has exceeded the amount originally granted and prior approval of the Public Accounts Committee is required
x: An excess grant is required when expenditure has exceeded the amount granted. It requires prior scrutiny and approval by the Public Accounts Committee.

s: With which of the following is a token grant associated?
o: An emergency demand of indefinite magnitude
A fresh withdrawal from the Public Account without parliamentary approval
A reduction of a Demand for Grant to Re 1
Re-appropriation and approval by the Lok Sabha
x: A token grant relates to re-appropriation and must also be voted by the Lok Sabha.

s: What is an exceptional grant?
o: Provides an advance for the first two months of the year
Is not part of the current service of any year
Is sanctioned after expenditure has exceeded the grant
Meets a new service not included in the Budget
x: An exceptional grant is made for a purpose that is not part of the current service of any financial year.

s: What is a Vote of Credit?
o: An advance grant for part of the financial year pending budget passage
A statutory authorization to withdraw voted grants from the Consolidated Fund
An unexpected, blank-check grant for an emergency or an indefinite demand
A grant reduced to ₹100 to ventilate a specific grievance
x: A vote of credit is an emergency grant, like a blank cheque, for a need whose details cannot be stated in the budget. Option A describes a vote on account.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Supplementary grant – sanctioned amount is insufficient
Excess grant – expenditure exceeds the amount already granted
Additional grant – sanctioned amount is insufficient
Vote of credit – unexpected demand of indefinite magnitude or character
x: An additional grant covers a new service not included in the Budget; insufficiency is met by a supplementary grant.

s: For what is an additional grant under Article 115 sanctioned?
o: An emergency whose details cannot be stated
A new service not in the Budget
x: An additional grant is for a new service not in the Budget; a supplementary grant is for an insufficient amount.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Article 115 covers supplementary, additional and excess grants; Article 116 covers vote on account, vote of credit and exceptional grants.

s: Which committee must approve an excess grant before the Lok Sabha votes it?
x: An excess grant needs the approval of the Public Accounts Committee first.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Vote on Account?
x: Article 116 provides for the Vote on Account, a grant in advance for part of the year until the Budget is passed.
